title: Hashamomuk
summary: Hashamomuk is William Wallace Tooker's name for a neck of land west of Greenport in Southold. Later entries connect the place with Nashayonsuck, a brook-boundary name, and with neighboring Southold forms such as Monnepaught and Caushawasha.
address_label: Hashamomuk / Arshamomaque area west of Greenport, Southold, NY
history_content: Hashamomuk connects a brook, swamp, pond, boundary names, and related North Fork land records. Dated documentary details appear in the Historic Timeline with their own sources.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Hashamomuk, Hashamomuck, Arshamomaque, Harshamomogue, Arshamomague, Nashayonsuck, Nassayonsuck, and Neshugguncer. Arshamomaque and Harshamomogue are handled as alternate forms of the same Southold/Greenport landscape. Nashayonsuck is interpreted as the fork of the brook or outlet, or a place between the forks of a brook. The main Hashamomuk meaning remains uncertain.

Why Place Names Matter

“Whenever people of any sort, from ancient to modern times, come into a land that is new to them, they begin at once to name their surroundings. This is something that cannot wait.”

— Constance Mary Matthews, How Placenames Began and How They Develop (1974), Quoted in UNGEGN Media Kit 12, PDF page 1

Place-name history should show Native people as active and present, not only as names in old documents.
land_loss_content: Hashamomuk gathers together a dense Indigenous geography of neck, creek, swamp, pond, and boundary names around Greenport and Southold. Treating it as a primary placename helps keep those related names connected rather than scattered as isolated fragments.
whereintheworld_content: Tooker associates Hashamomuk with the neck west of Greenport. Nashayonsuck, Tom's Creek, Caushawasha, Minnapaugs, Patchummuck, Paucuckatux, and Sonnquoquas remain part of the wider Southold and Greenport place-name landscape; exact historic boundaries remain uncertain.
